name: Theme toggle
description: An icon button that switches between a dark and a light theme and remembers the choice. The moon or sun shows from CSS alone, following the colour scheme, so it's right on first paint.
whenToUse: A site or app header where readers pick light or dark.
whenNotToUse: Choosing between more than two themes, or "system" — use a Select or radio group with setTheme().
Theming one section — set data-theme on it.

classes.ayy-theme-toggle: On the button (with ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--icon). Stacks the two icons.

js: themeToggleClass, themeToggleMoonClass, themeToggleSunClass constants; connectThemeToggle(button, { dark?, light?, onChange? }) → cleanup.

attributes.dark: dark | dark-soft — theme to switch to for dark
attributes.light: light | light-gray — theme to switch to for light

events.ayy-value-change: { value: string } — the theme just applied

element.children: One <button> with both icons. aria-pressed (true while dark) is kept in sync for you, including when the OS preference changes.

ThemeToggle.renders: <button class="ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--icon ayy-theme-toggle"> with both icons

a11y: A toggle button: a fixed name ("Dark theme") and aria-pressed="true" while dark, so screen readers announce the state.
The icons are aria-hidden; the name and state carry the meaning.
do: Add themeInitScript to <head> so the stored theme applies before first paint.
Put it next to the brand or before the call to action in the Navbar.
dont: Don't change the label with the state; aria-pressed already says it.
